e-21543.knowledge_point: Identifying the Form of a Particular Solution for Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
e-21543.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/c9810bd07c9da4bd3d803740a85ce484cd92f4a0d8cb73af75d53602f8611a72.png)
A complementary solution to this system is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/85139452af923a4f7b793fc47454cb99579ce0fa68ae33de3a15747501f624ef.png)
Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $\mathbf{x}(t)=\mathbf{x}_c(t)+\mathbf{x}_p(t),$ where $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution $\mathbf{x}_p(t).$
e-21543.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
\mathbf{x}(t)=\mathbf{x}_c(t)+\mathbf{x}_p(t)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_c(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/13785393b66b769c10efcbf7cf9f1bb4f05c412a1ddb8649427b659728c7bd3e.png)
of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/4b2dbbf0847dc9ea9f438e3848dca79da5f4e3f4473ab325a5f2c48e8b77e98c.png)
where $a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2$ are constants that are to be determined.

e-21540.knowledge_point: Finding the Particular Solution of an Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
e-21540.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/eaf224db946e02695b83465fa548948a27e7587c7d4b270c604c897cdd4a2228.png)
The complementary solution to this system is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/b7ae867ae694152125bc8cdf1ee7ab34c52b0c050408db3d2da86c7cbbc88493.png)
Find the general solution of the system.
e-21540.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{x}_c(t) + \mathbf{x}_p(t)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_c(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/c68bfa253f23fb2c116b8769744e6fd22b7b898047e3ef3fe97f66dd91fefaa1.png)
of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also exponential, i.e.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/b270d56283fdced6971e1a00fc3e642e379fc9348a0e4fb17a97ba6db2d8fc13.png)
where $a,b$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of $\mathbf{x}_p$ with respect to $t$ gives
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/ca497159ae72a8b87997c78815119bb3de53782878cb2209072dcc505c902f37.png)

To find the unknown constants, we substitute $\mathbf{x}_p$ and $\mathbf{x}'_p$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}7{e}^{7t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {e}^{7t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+{e}^{7t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ 7[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}7a \\ 7b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3a+b \\ b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}7a \\ 7b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3a+b-1 \\ b-3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3a+b-1=7a \\ b-3=7b\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get 

$$
b - 7b = 3
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
b = -\dfrac12.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $a,$ we have

$$
3a - \dfrac12 - 1 = 7a
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
a = -\dfrac38.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/fff596d40155dc7787910405557a722b5258890e3fae88f60842de92fac47177.png)

And thus, the general solution is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/dc74c06c84905f8490932369e24cecd8f3b7eb64fdc4413e42c2f8bc1a3f3cbd.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/5b0bb8069abe99949fc52c0be82c22f5879d7ca0ac334af396f47efa41ae0b5e.png)
Find the missing coefficients in the solution to the initial value problem, shown above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/f220005265275c9297b7beef58777203a94351cb4957a26ca630802664759dc5.png)
e-21541.worked_solution:
We are told that the general solution to the system is 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/40f93d12ebe4519dc4aa15f0df4b568ffa25f25afd99ec45130b569083c21fe0.png)
where $c_1,c_2$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Next, we find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2.$ Substituting $t = 0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{0} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0\cdot {e}^{0} \\ {e}^{0}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}-0+4 \\ -{0}^{2}+2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+4 \\ {c}_{2}+2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+4=6 \\ {c}_{2}+2=1\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get $c_1 = 2.$ From the second equation, we have $c_2 = -1.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/948088eb5d495f3d8a8a96f038b5b036b53fa398544f9faedbb08026e96b661e.png)

before.name: Question 6
before.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$

Question 6
?

Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: x′(t)=[0−550]x(t)+cos⁡(7t)[21] A complementary solution to this system is given by xc(t)=c1[cos⁡(5t)sin⁡(5t)]+c2[−sin⁡(5t)cos⁡(5t)],c1,c2∈R. Then, the general solution of the system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t), where xp(t) is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution xp(t).

a
e5t(cos⁡(7t)[a1a2]+sin⁡(7t)[b1b2])
b
e5tcos⁡(7t)[a1a2]
c
cos⁡(7t)[a1a2]+sin⁡(7t)[b1b2]
d
cos⁡(5t)[b1b2]
e
cos⁡(5t)[a1a2]+sin⁡(5t)[b1b2]
Submit

decision.explanation: The forcing has frequency 7, distinct from the homogeneous frequency 5, so use a cosine-and-sine trial at frequency 7 without a resonance factor. Substitution verifies that a=(-5/24,5/12)^T and b=(7/12,7/24)^T give a particular solution of option c's form.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]+\operatorname{sin}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: x′(t)=[0−550]x(t)+cos⁡(7t)[21] A complementary solution to this system is given by xc(t)=c1[cos⁡(5t)sin⁡(5t)]+c2[−sin⁡(5t)cos⁡(5t)],c1,c2∈R. Then, the general solution of the system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t), where xp(t) is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution xp(t).

a
e5t(cos⁡(7t)[a1a2]+sin⁡(7t)[b1b2])
b
e5tcos⁡(7t)[a1a2]
c

EXPLANATION

Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t) where xc(t) is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and xp(t) is a particular solution.

The forcing term cos⁡(7t)[21] of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e. xp(t)=cos⁡(7t)[a1a2]+sin⁡(7t)[b1b2], where a1,a2,b1,b2 are constants that are to be determined.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Form of a Particular Solution for Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
content.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]+\operatorname{sin}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

before.name: Question 7
before.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}(t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]){e}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$

Question 7
?

Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: x′(t)=[1101]x(t)+sin⁡(6t)[−13] The complementary solution to this system is given by xc(t)=c1[10]et+c2(t[10]+[01])et,c1,c2∈R. Then, the general solution of the system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t), where xp(t) is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution xp(t).

a
et(cos⁡(6t)[a1a2]+sin⁡(6t)[b1b2])
b
etsin⁡(6t)[a1a2]
c
sin⁡(6t)[b1b2]
d
etcos⁡(6t)[b1b2]
e
cos⁡(6t)[a1a2]+sin⁡(6t)[b1b2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Use both cosine and sine at the forcing frequency 6 because differentiation interchanges them. The matrix has only eigenvalue 1, so there is no resonance with ±6i and no extra exponential or t factor is needed. Substituting x_p=a cos(6t)+b sin(6t) gives 6b=Aa and -6a=Ab+(-1,3)^T; these equations are solvable since A²+36I is invertible.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}(t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]){e}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]+\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

EXPLANATION

Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t) where xc(t) is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and xp(t) is a particular solution.

The forcing term sin⁡(6t)[−13] of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e. xp(t)=cos⁡(6t)[a1a2]+sin⁡(6t)[b1b2], where a1,a2,b1,b2 are constants that are to be determined.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option e: both cosine and sine at frequency 6 are needed, with no exponential factor. There is no resonance because the system's only eigenvalue is 1. The deliberately incorrect submission selected d; the earlier prediction e remains correct.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Form of a Particular Solution for Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
content.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}(t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]){e}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]+\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

before.name: Question 8
before.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+2t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+2t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+2t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is a polynomial in $t$ of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree $2$, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

EXPLANATION

Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t) where xc(t) is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and xp(t) is a particular solution.

The forcing term [t2+2t+3−t2+2t] of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is a polynomial in t of degree 2. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree 2, i.e. xp(t)=t2[a1a2]+t[b1b2]+[c1c2], where a1,a2,b1,b2,c1,c2 are constants that are to be determined.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Form of a Particular Solution for Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
content.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+2t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+2t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is a polynomial in $t$ of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree $2$, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

before.name: Question 9
before.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as 
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$
where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$

Question 9
?

Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: x′(t)=[0−330]x(t)+e2t[4−1] A complementary solution to this system is given by xc(t)=c1[cos⁡(3t)sin⁡(3t)]+c2[−sin⁡(3t)cos⁡(3t)],c1,c2∈R. Then, the general solution of the system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t), where xp(t) is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution xp(t).

b

c

e

decision.explanation: Use x_p(t)=e^{2t}a. Substitution gives (2I-A)a=(4,-1)^T, yielding a=(11/13,10/13)^T. Thus option a contains a valid particular solution; no resonance factor is needed.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as 
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$
where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution has the same exponential factor, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t), where xp(t) is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution xp(t).

EXPLANATION

Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as x(t)=xc(t)+xp(t) where xc(t) is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and xp(t) is a particular solution.

The forcing term e2t[4−1] of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution has the same exponential factor, i.e. xp(t)=e2t[a1a2], where a1,a2 are constants that are to be determined.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Form of a Particular Solution for Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
content.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as 
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$
where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution has the same exponential factor, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

before.name: Question 10
before.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{5} & -\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{1}{5} & -\frac{7}{5}\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}(t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]){e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as 
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$
where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$

Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2t+1 \\ 8t\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is a polynomial of degree $1.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree $1,$ i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}])+[\begin{aligned}-2t+1 \\ 8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} \\ -2{a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{2} \\ -2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2t+1 \\ 8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0t+{a}_{1} \\ 0t+{a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}({a}_{2}-2)t+({b}_{2}+1) \\ (-2{a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}+8)t+(-2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2})\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{a}_{2}-2=0 \\ -2{a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}+8=0 \\ {b}_{2}+1={a}_{1} \\ -2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2}={a}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first two equations, we get 

$$
{a}_{2}=2,\,{a}_{1}=1.
$$

 
Substituting these into the third and fourth equations, and solving for ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2},$ we have

$$
{b}_{2}=0,\,{b}_{1}=-1.
$$

 

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
